title: Bounded Rationality
hook: Trying to account for every variable is how a two-day decision turns into two months.
statement: Narrow the scope of a problem so you can actually make a good decision.
explainer: Considering everything feels responsible, but complexity grows faster than your brain can keep up. A clear, smaller scope beats a complete one that never gets decided.
sop: Write down every variable you're trying to account for.
Score Scope and Complexity from 1 to 10, then for a narrower version.
Draw a hard line around what you'll consider. Ignore the rest on purpose.
Decide inside that line with what you know now.
Revisit if new info changes things, but don't wait for it.
equation_example: Scope 8 ÷ Complexity 4 = 2.0. That's a decision you can actually make. Scope 3 ÷ Complexity 9 = 0.33, which is overwhelm. Higher means a clean, doable call. Lower means you're trying to solve too much at once.
question: Write down one problem you're stuck on and the smaller version you'll solve first.
closing_statement: A narrower problem is usually a solvable one.
caption:
Principle Nº 221: Bounded Rationality

Trying to account for every variable is how a two-day decision turns into two months.

Narrow the scope of a problem so you can actually make a good decision.

Your turn: Write down one problem you're stuck on and the smaller version you'll solve first.
